title: Learn to Spot FAKE MUSCLES (Abs, A$$ & Chest Implants)
summary: NH explains how to spot cosmetic muscle implants (abs, glutes, chest) increasingly common on Instagram, using Liver King, French influencer David Michigan and Rich Piana as examples. He argues implants, like PEDs, give the look without the health, strength or inner value of training, feed body dysmorphia and repeat surgery, and that you should not take advice from people who bought their bodies.
claims: Steroid muscle is real muscle that fades off cycle; synthol is oil that inflates the muscle; implants are permanent and increasingly realistic
Someone with implants failed to build the muscle themselves, so they are a poor source of training advice
Pro bodybuilders rarely use implants because implants lack striations, cannot flex and look out of place on stage; they prefer site injections or synthol
Ab implants are slid over the rectus through a side incision, often with fat removed between the bellies, so they bulge unnaturally far from the skin
Signs of ab implants: abs on a protruding gut, abs that look identical year after year and do not stretch or move with the body, and a bolted-on look
Real abs come with lower body fat and a stronger core; implants give neither
Abs out of proportion with real strength are a red flag; he cites Liver King's weak overhead press with suspicious plates versus Eddie Hall, whose six-pack reflects a hugely strong core
David Michigan, a French influencer he calls the French Liver King, shows bolted-on abs beside love handles and lower-belly fat, a sign of liposuction plus ab implants
Masculinity-market influencers all look alike (beards, cigars, bikini girls) and exploit primitive instincts to sell products
Ab implant surgery costs around $10,000 in New York and less elsewhere; before-and-after photos show untrained skinny-fat men
Natural bodybuilding is not a vanity pursuit because the work teaches discipline and sacrifice and improves health; implants and PEDs give the look without the internal value
Implants, like PEDs, remove the incentive to fix diet and lifestyle; recipients often eat worse afterwards
One cosmetic surgery tends to lead to more; implants also need replacing roughly every 10 years and age badly
Lifting satisfies you through accomplishment; purchased bodies never fill the void and create dependence like PEDs do
Anecdote: a woman at his commercial gym returned from Brazil with butt implants that looked absurd on her frame; he could see the implant shape when she squatted
Signs of butt implants: glute size that contradicts squat strength (a big natural butt can usually squat two plates) and big glutes on tiny legs
Glute exercises also train quads and hamstrings, so natural glutes come with developed legs; implants may cause the surrounding muscle to atrophy
Butt implants cost about $5,000 in the US and $2,000 in Brazil
A strong posterior chain protects older women from hip and back injuries; implants discourage training it
Any woman doing squats, deadlifts and glute work in a caloric surplus will build big glutes; women are designed to store fat and muscle there
Getting implants signals an unresolved complex or body dysmorphia; surgeons profit from the spiral
He believes Rich Piana had chest, arm and ab implants and advanced body dysmorphia, though he loved him
Beginners judge advice by size, ignoring PEDs and implants; influencers exploit that to buy social proof
You can buy a nice body now through hormones and implants, so judge role models on their inner values, discipline and beliefs, not their abs
